rfm_tuples.M_value: Covenants struck Aug 21, 2025: max Consolidated Leverage Ratio = 4.50x (years 1-3) stepping to 4.25x; min Consolidated Interest Coverage Ratio = 3.00x. UNCHANGED from prior covenant levels — NO covenant relaxation between FY25 and Q1 2026. Term Loan A bears 6.87% effective; Term Loan B at 8.43%. Total drawn debt approximately $2.78B; revolver availability $596.6M; cash $169.8M = approximately $766M total liquidity. FY25 Adjusted EBITDA segment-level North America $807M + other segments roughly $275M = ~$1,082M, minus corporate ~$534M = ~$548M consolidated Adj EBITDA. Net leverage proxy: $2.78B drawn - $169.8M cash = $2.61B / $548M EBITDA = ~4.77x. This is ABOVE the 4.50x covenant on a simple calc, suggesting Credit Agreement EBITDA definition includes addbacks (restructuring, integration, impairments) that bring covenant leverage down — the company says they ARE compliant. Q1 2026 interest expense $51.1M annualized $204M = ICR ~$548M/$204M = 2.69x — BELOW the 3.00x covenant on a simple calc. Again, the covenant calc almost certainly adds back items, but headroom is thin.

They struck a new Credit Agreement on standard 4.50x / 3.00x terms in Aug 2025 (during the deep impairment cycle) and they remain in compliance through Q1 2026. Simple-math leverage is tight (~4.8x gross), implying the covenant calc relies on EBITDA addbacks — but the lenders accepted the credit at standard terms. This is NEUTRAL evidence: not a tailwind, but not a red flag either. Contrast: MOH had to drop ICR from 3.0 to 1.75 just days before the 10-K. QDEL's covenants held at 3.0x ICR / 4.5x leverage and management asserts compliance both at fiscal year-end and Q1 2026.

summary: QDEL stands out as the STRONGEST Form 4 insider-PURCHASE signal in the forward-test cohort. Six named officers/directors — CEO Brian J. Blaser ($750K across two prints), CFO Joseph M. Busky ($304K across two prints), Director Matthew Strobeck ($240K single trade), plus three independent directors (Polan/Wilkins/Rhoads $54K combined) — executed TEN code-P open-market purchases totaling $1.61M between Nov 19 2025 and Feb 13 2026 with ZERO offsetting officer/director sales. CEO Blaser's $502K purchase on Nov 19 2025 fell six days before the Q3 print and his $249K Feb 13 follow-on was six days after Q4 — both discretionary (Item 9B confirms NO 10b5-1 plans were active in Q4 2025). Carlyle's $447M of selling is fully explained as 2024 post-Combinations 10pct-holder distribution (zero Carlyle Form 4s in 2025 or 2026) and not informed-selling. Operationally the story is honest-distress: FY25 net loss -$1.13B but driven by $700.7M goodwill impairment + $149.7M SAVANNA Exit charge + $9.7M asset impairment; operating cash flow positive $105M; new Credit Agreement struck Aug 21 2025 at STANDARD 4.50x leverage / 3.00x ICR covenants (no relaxation vs prior — contrast MOH which had to cut ICR to 1.75x days before its 10-K); material weakness from FY24 fully remediated with KPMG unqualified ICFR opinion; auditor unchanged. Q1 2026 weak (-10.5% revenue YoY, $91.8M net loss) driven by Grifols Joint Business termination ($65M one-time) + weak respiratory season (-30% ILI per CDC). Bristol County securities class action (SAVANNA RVP4 / COVID statements) pending motion to dismiss but current CEO Blaser NOT named (he started May 2024). The composite Form-4 evidence — six discretionary insider buyers including CEO + CFO into the trough at $21-28/share, no covenant relaxation, clean material-weakness remediation — places QDEL squarely in the 'distressed-but-honest with insider conviction' bucket. LONG-tier.
